title: Reverse a LL [Recursive]
stepTitle: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
category: Learn LinkedList [Single LL, Double LL, Medium, Hard Problems]
pattern: reverse the rest, then fix one edge
problemStatement: Reverse a singly linked list recursively.
intuition: Assume the suffix after head is already reversed. Then you only need to make head.next point back at head and cut head off the front.

approaches.title: Recursive reversal
approaches.idea: Base case: empty or single node. Then rewire two pointers on the way back up.
approaches.code:
def reverse_list_rec(head):
    if head is None or head.next is None:
        return head
    new_head = reverse_list_rec(head.next)
    head.next.next = head
    head.next = None
    return new_head
approaches.spaceNote: Stack depth equals list length — a real memory cost, unlike the iterative version
approaches.whyWorks: head.next is the tail of the reversed suffix, so pointing it at head appends head correctly.

commonMistakes: Forgetting head.next = None, which creates a cycle
patternRecognition: "Solve the suffix, then fix one local connection"
followUps: Compare stack cost with the iterative version
Reverse in groups of k recursively
interviewInsight: Stating the O(n) stack cost out loud prevents the "so it is O(1) space?" trap.
